Date July 7, 1938.

Subject Request by Mr. T.K. Ho in connection with arrests
in national salvation activities.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Mr. T. K. Ho of the Secretariat informed D.I.
Crawford by phone that he had been approached by Mr. T.T.
Cheu (also known as Tseu Pang Tsing (周邦俊)), a member of
the Health Committee of the S.M.C. and Manager of the
Great China Dispensary, Foochow Road, that detectives
from the Special Branch were still looking for Tseu Vung
Ziang (周文祥), the son of Mr. T.T. Cheu and asked if it
was possible to withdraw the detectives so instructed,
as Mr. T.T. Cheu was prepared to submit a personal guarantee
for the good behaviour of his son, a procedure, he believed,
which had been adopted in the case of two arrests made in
the same case.

Mr. Ho also requested that literature seized at
Mr. T.T. Cheu's home at Lane 118, 120 Yates Road, also
be returned which had not been proved to be anti-Japanese
or national salvation nature. A perusal of the few papers
and unity magazines show that all the literature taken
away by the Police was definitely of national salvation
nature, but as to the first proposal by Mr. Ho, this person
has come to the notice of the Police on three different
occasions as having been actively connected with national
salvation associations and everything points towards him
being a responsible member of an organization directing
the action of those national salvation associations.

C. Crawford
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)

主题：何先生（Mr. T.K. Ho）就涉及救国活动逮捕一事提出的请求。

制作及转呈人：巡官克劳福德（D.I. Crawford）

秘书处何先生（Mr. T. K. Ho）通过电话告知巡官克劳福德，工部局卫生委员会委员兼福州路中西大药房经理周邦俊先生（Mr. T.T. Cheu，又名 Tseu Pang Tsing (周邦俊)）曾与其接洽，称特务科侦探仍在搜寻周邦俊之子周文祥（Tseu Vung Ziang (周文祥)），并询问是否可能撤回受命执行此任务的侦探，因为周邦俊先生愿意为其子的良好行为提交个人担保，他认为此前在同一案件的两起逮捕中曾采用过此程序。

何先生还要求归还从周邦俊先生位于亚尔培路120弄118号家中搜获的文献，据称这些文献未被证实具有抗日或救国性质。经查阅少量报纸和《团结》杂志，显示警方带走的所有文献确属救国性质，但就何先生的第一项提议而言，此人已三次引起警方注意，因其积极参与救国团体，且所有迹象表明他是指挥这些救国团体行动的组织中的负责成员。

June 15, 1938.

NIPPO

COMMUNISTS AND ANTI-JAPANESE ELEMENTS ARRESTED

On the morning of June 10 the
authorities concerned carried out a raid at the Kuohwa
Middle School, No. 1163 Gordon Road and arrested seven
students including one named Chou. They are now
undergoing examination. According to information
received, they are communists and anti-Japanese elements
who have been actively engaged in encouraging Chinese
students to proceed to Hankow for military service.
They were about to leave Shanghai for Hankow. The
authorities are reported to have seized a large quantity
of anti-Japanese literature and two pistols.

Subject Re attached

Made by D.S.I. Burton. Forwarded by [签名] Inspt. 1/c.

Sir,

With reference to the attached report appearing
in the Ta Mei Wan Pao (大美晚报), date June 13th, 1938 (morning
translation), stating that a male Chinese student named Chu (朱)
together with 6 other students, had been arrested by the
Japanese Authorities on the morning of June 10th, 1938, at the
Kuo Hwa Middle School, No. 1163 Gordon Road, there is definitely
no truth in the report whatsoever.

The undersigned visited the said school and there
interviewed one Ho Sz Tun (何士敦), deputy principal of the
school, who stated that Japanese have never visited the school,
nor had any of the pupils been arrested, but he had heard that
an ex-student of the school named Chu Shui (朱水) had been
arrested, but by whom he did not know.

He further stated that on the afternoon of 14.6.38.,
he visited Police Headquarters, where he interviewed a Chinese
whom he told that there was no truth in the article appearing
in the Ta Mei Wan Pao, and asked whether this article would
injure the reputation of the school or not, he was told by the
Chinese that he had better write to the paper refuting the
article and request them to publish a correct, this he did
on his return to the school.

The man Chu referred to in the newspaper article is
the aforementioned Chu Shui, who was arrested at 6 p.m. on the
10.6.38 at No. 4, Lane No. 234 Mapai Road, by D.S. Pitts of the
Special Branch, see Special Branch File D. 8540/38.

[签名]
D.S.I.

D.D.O. "B" Division.

主题：关于附件

制作人：副总督察伯顿（D.S.I. Burton）。转呈人：[签名] 督察长。

先生，

关于附件中刊登于1938年6月13日《大美晚报》（Ta Mei Wan Pao）的报道（晨版译文），称一名姓朱（Chu）的中国男学生连同其他6名学生，于1938年6月10日上午在戈登路1163号国华中学被日本当局逮捕，该报道绝无事实依据。

签署人走访了该校，并会见了该校副校长何士敦（Ho Sz Tun），后者表示日本人从未到过该校，也没有任何学生被捕，但他听说该校一名名叫朱水（Chu Shui）的 former 学生被捕，但不知是被谁所捕。

他还表示，1938年6月14日下午，他前往警察总局，会见了一名华人，他向该华人表示《大美晚报》刊登的文章不实，并询问该文章是否会损害学校声誉，该华人告诉他最好写信给报社反驳该文章，并要求他们刊登更正声明，他回到学校后便照做了。

报纸文章中提到的朱姓男子即上述朱水，他于1938年6月10日下午6时在马派路234弄4号被特务科警佐皮茨（D.S. Pitts）逮捕，见特务科档案 D. 8540/38。

[签名]

Branch dated 15-6-38
Date June 15th 1938

Subject Alleged arrests of seven Chinese students by Japanese Authorities -
press report.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Sau-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford D.J.

With reference to the attached press translation
from the Ta Mei Wan Pao of June 13th regarding the arrests
by the Japanese Authorities of seven Chinese students from
the Kuo Hwa Middle School, 1163 Gordon Road (Pootoo Road
District) on June 10th: Mr. Woo Sz Dung (胡思屯), a
responsible faculty member of the above school, was interview-
ed at Headquarters on June 14th. He stated that there was
no truth in the press report as no arrests had ever been
made in the school premises, nor has the school ever been
visited by the Japanese Authorities, but, Mr. Woo added, that
he had heard a rumour that one Tsu Taieu (朱修), a
newly graduated student from the above school, had been
arrested by the Japanese Authorities about one week ago and
his present whereabouts were unknown.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 15 JUNE 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

In endeavouring to trace this rumour it was found
that it referred to Tsu Tsieu who was arrested by the
Municipal Police at 6 p.m. on June 3rd at 4/234 Mapai Road
in connection with the distribution of the booklet "Unity".
(vide Special Branch report dated June 3rd under the heading:
Anti-Japanese and Communistic publication). This person is
at present detained in Central Station and is under interroga-
tion by detectives from Special Branch.

D.C. (Special Branch).

（签名：Shih / D.S.I.）

（批：d.b.r. / 15/6）
F. A. to D. C. (S. B.)

主题：据报日本当局逮捕七名中国学生——新闻报道。

制作人：副总督察施绍坚（D.S.I. Shih Sau-chien） 转呈人：C. 克劳福德 副督察长。

关于附件中1938年6月13日《大美晚报》的新闻译文，涉及日本当局于6月10日在戈登路1163号（普陀路分区）国华中学逮捕七名中国学生一事：上述学校的负责教职员胡思屯先生（Mr. Woo Sz Dung）于6月14日在总局接受问询。他表示新闻报道不实，因为校内从未发生过逮捕事件，日本当局也从未造访过该校，但胡先生补充说，他听到谣言称该校一名应届毕业生朱修（Tsu Taieu (朱修)）约一周前被日本当局逮捕，目前下落不明。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1938年6月15日 / 特务科）

在试图追踪这一谣言时，发现其指的是朱修（Tsu Tsieu），他因分发《团结》小册子于6月3日下午6时在马派路234弄4号被工部局警务处逮捕。（参见6月3日特务科报告，标题为：抗日及共产主义出版物）。此人目前拘押在中央捕房，正接受特务科侦探的审讯。

副总监（特务科）。

June 14, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao dated June 13 :-

JAPANESE ARREST SEVEN CHINESE STUDENTS

According to reports from reliable
sources, a student named Chu (朱) and six others
were arrested by the Japanese authorities at the Kuo
Hwa Middle School (國華中學), No. 1163 Gordon Road,
on the morning of June 10. Most of these arrested
students are youths of 16 to 17 years of age. At the
time of their arrest, two pistols, two swords and a
quantity of anti-Japanese literature were found and seized.
Nothing is known of the fate of these seven students.
It is learned that they are all full-
blooded patriots who were about to proceed to Hankow
for the summer vacation. This was discovered by the
Japanese authorities and the students were arrested.
The matter is receiving particular
attention from the public. When interviewed by our
reporter, the school authorities denied that these
seven students had been arrested at the Kuo Hwa Middle
School.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISS... 14 JUNE 1938）
page_data.zh:
1938年6月14日。晨版译文。

6月13日《大美晚报》：-

日本逮捕七名中国学生

据可靠消息来源报道，6月10日上午，一名姓朱（Chu）的学生及其他六人在戈登路1163号国华中学（國華中學）被日本当局逮捕。这些被捕学生大多是16至17岁的青年。逮捕时，现场发现并缴获了两支手枪、两把剑和大量抗日文献。这七名学生的命运尚不清楚。据悉，他们都是满腔热血的爱国者，正准备利用暑假前往汉口。此事被日本当局察觉，学生们遂被捕。
此事正受到公众的特别关注。当本报记者采访校方时，校方否认这七名学生是在国华中学被捕的。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处处... 1938年6月14日）

REPORT
Date June 17, 1938.

Subject Anti-Japanese Literature - disposal of prisoner

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford R.I

In accordance with the attached instructions of
the D.C. (Special Branch) dated June 15, 1938, prisoner
Yuan Ken-sung was escorted to the Roosevelt Terminal
during the afternoon of June 16, 1938 by D.S. Pitts and
C.D.C.30 and there placed on board the s.s. "Comandante
Paolini," which left for Wenchow at 3.20 p.m. Prior
to being deported the prisoner was warned that should he
return to Shanghai and engage in further political
activities he would not be dealt with so leniently.

Tsiang Pah-sung and Tsu Sieu, the other individuals
detained, were handed over to their respective fathers at
5 p.m. June 16 after the attached bonds had been furnished
by the parents and a guarantor, by which they assume full
responsibility for the future good behaviour of the two
youths. Before being released, C.D.I. Ross cautioned
both individuals as to their future conduct, warning them
not to indulge in further political activities.

（左侧印章：SPECIAL BRANCH）

Ja. Pitts'
D. S.

制作人：警佐皮茨（D.S. Pitts） 转呈人：C. 克劳福德 督察长

根据1938年6月15日特务科副总监的附件指令，犯人袁根松（Yuan Ken-sung）于1938年6月16日下午由警佐皮茨和刑事侦缉队30号（C.D.C.30）护送至罗斯福码头，并登上将于下午3点20分启程前往温州的“保洛尼指挥官”号（s.s. "Comandante Paolini"）轮船。在被驱逐出境前，警告该犯人，若其返回上海并继续从事政治活动，将不会如此宽大处理。

另外两名被拘留者蒋柏松（Tsiang Pah-sung）和朱修（Tsu Sieu），在其父母及担保人提供附件所示保证书后，于6月16日下午5时交予各自的父亲，由他们承担这两名青年今后行为良好的全部责任。在释放前，刑事侦缉督察罗斯（C.D.I. Ross）对两人的未来行为进行了告诫，警告他们不要沉溺于进一步的政治活动。

（左侧印章：特务科）

Date : June 16, 1938.

My son, Tsu Sieu aged 20, a native
of Pootung, and a student of the Kuo Hwa Middle School,
corner of Gordon and Robison Roads, having been engaged
in the distribution of anti-Japanese literature, was
arrested by the Municipal Police and will now be released
on a guarantee hereby given by me. I guarantee that the
above-mentioned Tsu Sieu will in future refrain
from all National Salvation activities or anti-Japanese
activities and will confine himself to matters entirely
unconnected with any political movement while he stays
in Shanghai.

Signed : Tsu Vee-jáh
Address : 212 Penang Road, O.O.L.
Position : Unemployed.

REPORT    Date June 14, 1938.

Subject Anti-Japanese Literature.

Made by D.S. Pitts    Forwarded by C. Crawford S.J.

In regard to the contents of the attached file,
further attempts made by this office to effect the arrest
of those persons implicated by the three individuals now
detained, as being responsible for the supplying and
distributing of anti-Japanese literature and booklets,
have up to the present been unsuccessful and according to
enquiries made it would appear that these wanted men have
left Shanghai for Hankow and/or other ports farther afield.

Detectives have maintained a watch at ——

(1) The Chinese Y.M.C.A. Western Social Centre, Robison Road;
(2) House 9, Lane 234 Kapai Road;
(3) house 120, Lane 214 Yates Road, but no sign has been
observed of any communication agents, of any person in
possession or suspected of being in possession of subversive
literature, of Tong Shao Tseng (廖少真), of one Zung
(陈 ) or of Tseu Vung Ziang (周文祥).. The remaining
addresses mentioned in the attached reports have also been
made the subject of discreet enquiries, but nothing can be
learned that would assist in furthering our investigations
in this present case.

In view of the fact that it is not believed that any
more arrests will be made, the various watches are being
withdrawn to-day, but occasional visits will be paid to
the premises concerned in case of future activity.

is of interest to note that the person who lived there,

Tseu Vung Ziang, is known to this office as a member of
the National Crisis Education Society. On September 6,
1936 he was arrested and taken to Sinza Station for
participating in a movement the object of which was to
collect funds for National Salvation purposes. He was
subsequently released. In the latter part of March 1938
information was received which implicated him as being
concerned in the distribution of the anti-Japanese
publication "Unity." Tseu Vung Ziang is the son of
Mr. Tseu Tsing Tsing (周孝俊), General Manager of the
Great China Dispensary, 513 Foochow Road, and a committee
member of the Shanghai Municipal Council.

    It will be remembered that the initial information
in this case referred to the distribution of anti-Japanese
literature and the surreptitious sale of same through the
medium of street newsvendors. Steps have been taken to pre-
vent any such further sales and in addition to obtaining bonds
from certain newsvendors guaranteeing that they will refrain
from retailing political publications in future, other
newsvendors have been visited and warned not to deal in
similar literature. These steps, it is hoped, will act
as a deterrent to this manner of disseminating such literature.

    In regard to the three arrested persons,
(1) Yuan Ken Sung (袁耕莘), aged 38.
(2) Tsiang Fah Sung (蒋伯中), aged 19.
(3) Tsu Sieu (朱修), aged 20,
who are now detained at Central Station, instructions are

Further interrogation of the three individuals
in custody has revealed the following details :-

(1) Tsiang Pah-sung

Some three years while studying in the Shanghai
Middle School on Kiaochow Road, Tsiang made the
acquaintance of several students who were keen on
promoting education and who were taking an active
part in the national salvation movement. Some
six of these students took part in a meeting
observing the May 30 Incident which was held in
the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow
Road in 1935.

In 1936 and 1937 Tsiang studied radio telegraphy
in a school on Rue Lafayette and did not engage in
national salvation affairs.

Following the outbreak of hostilities in August,
1937, he served in the now defunct 145th Refugee
Camp of the Shanghai Emergency Relief Committee,
Ferry Road, off Robison Road, as a "director" in
health and education tasks. Prior to the withdrawal
of the Chinese forces from Shanghai, the "directors"
took part in national salvation work as instructed by
the Relief Committee, but suspended such work after
the withdrawal of the Chinese troops. Tsiang worked
in this camp until January, 1938, when it then
removed to North Honan Road.

对三名在押人员的进一步审讯揭示了以下细节：

(1) 蒋伯松 (Tsiang Pah-sung)

大约三年前，蒋在胶州路上海中学就读时，结识了几名热衷于促进教育并积极参与救国运动的学生。其中约六名学生参加了1935年在北苏州路上海总商会举行的纪念五卅惨案的会议。

1936年和1937年，蒋在辣斐德路的一所学校学习无线电报务，未参与救国事务。

1937年8月战事爆发后，他在位于罗宾森路旁渡船路的上海急赈委员会第145难民收容所（现已解散）担任卫生和教育工作的“干事”。在中国军队撤离上海之前，“干事”们按照救济委员会的指示参与救国工作，但在中国军队撤离后停止了此类工作。蒋在该收容所工作至1938年1月，随后该所迁至河南北路。

    According to Wu Hung-yeu and Hwa Ngoeh, the
meeting place of the staff members of the Students'
Circles' National Salvation Association is the
Medhurst College, 34 Ferry Road.
    About two months ago, Tsiang began to receive
copies of "Unity" from Tseu Vung-ziang.  The number
ranged from one copy to three.
    At 2 p.m. May 29, Tsiang attended the home of
Tseu Vung-ziang, 120 Dah Chung Li, Yates Road.  He
produced a subscription book for funds for "Unity"
and asked Tsiang to contribute, whereupon the latter
gave him twenty cents.  Besides "Unity," Tseu also
gave him copies of the "Emancipation," "Labour" and
"Students' Life".  Sometimes he sent them to Tsiang's
house and on other occasions Tsiang went to fetch
them himself.
    As to the copies of "Unity" seized by the Police
from Tsiang's house, the latter states they were
brought to his home by Tsu Sieu (朱修) at 4 p.m.
June 3 with a view to having them stored.  Tsu
intended to distribute them among students of the
Kuo Wah Middle School, corner of Gordon and Robison
Roads.  Tsu Sieu is responsible for the distribution
of copies of the "Unity" and "Students' Life" to the
Kuo Wah students on behalf of the Students' Circles'
National Salvation Association.

Road, and a committee member of the Shanghai Municipal
Council for the years 1937 and 1938.

College.

Subject Anti-Japanese and communistic publications - further developments.

Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford

Further to a report dated May 31, 1938 on the subject
of anti-Japanese and communistic publications and in
accordance with the instructions of the D.C. (Special Branch)
appearing on the attached file, arrangements were made to ap-
prehend Dong Shao Tseng (唐少真), a responsible member
of the Labourers' Circles' National Salvation Association,
upon his proposed visit to the Y.M.C.A. Western District
Social Centre on June 2. His description was secured from
Yuan Ying Ching, the prisoner in custody, and detectives
placed in the Centre and in its vicinity, but although they
waited from 1 p.m. until past 8 p.m. no sign of Dong was
observed. Arrangements are being made to attempt to
effect his arrest through other channels, the results of
which will form the subject matter of a subsequent report.

During the morning of June 3, the prisoner Yuan was
escorted to 9/234 Mapai Road where, according to this
individual, one "Zung" was due to meet him at 10 a.m., but
although detectives of this office were placed in a very
discreet manner so as not to alarm any intending visitor to
the premises, "Zung" did not put in an appearance.

Agents and detectives however, were left in the neighbour-
hood of both the Y.M.C.A. Western District Social Centre and
Lane 234 Mapai Road with instructions to apprehend anybody
in possession or suspected of being in possession of
literature of an anti-Japanese or communistic nature.

In regard to the newsvendors mentioned in the report of
May 31 as being known to this office as retailers of anti-
Japanese literature, six of their stalls were visited during

继1938年5月31日关于反日及共产主义出版物的报告之后，并按照附件档案上特科主管（D.C.）的指示，已安排于6月2日劳工救国会负责人董少真（唐少真）拟访问青年会西区社会中心时将其逮捕。其体貌特征由在押犯人袁英庆（音译）提供，侦探被部署在该中心及其附近，尽管他们从下午1点一直守候到晚上8点以后，但未发现董的踪迹。正通过其他渠道安排试图实施逮捕，其结果将在后续报告中陈述。

6月3日上午，犯人袁被押送至马派路234弄9号，据该人称，一名“宗”姓男子定于上午10时在此与他见面，尽管本处侦探以非常谨慎的方式部署，以免惊动任何打算来访者，但“宗”并未出现。

然而，特工和侦探仍留守在青年会西区社会中心和马派路234弄附近，奉命逮捕任何持有或疑似持有反日或共产主义性质文献的人。

behaviour and strongly advised to warn this office of any
attempt made by strangers to induce them to retail literature
of a political aspect, they were released.

    At 4 p.m. June 3, C.D.C. 107 of this office - on
observation duty at Lane 234 Mapai Road - arrested one Tsiang
Pah Sung ( 蔣伯申 ), aged 19, a native of Shaoshing,
single, student, residing at 6/234 Mapai Road.    At the time
of being taken into custody he was in possession of two
copies of "Unity," one copy of "The Voice of War" and a
receipt for a contribution to the funds of "Unity."    C.D.C.
107 escorted this individual to Pootoo Road Station, which
in turn advised D.I. Crawford of what had transpired.    D.S.
Pitts, D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken and C.D.S. 89 attended and
interrogated the man who alleged that he had received the
literature and receipt from one Tsu Tsieu ( 朱脩 ), a
fellow student at the Kuo Hwa ( 國華 ) Middle School,
Gordon and Robison Roads corner during the same afternoon.
Tsiang declared that he did not know Tsu's home address but
that he (Tsiang) had been receiving copies of anti-Japanese
publications for the past two months and that some six or
seven such booklets were to be found at his (Tsiang's) home
at 6/234 Mapai Road.

With D.S.I. Chow (Pootoo Road Station), the above
mentioned party of Special Branch detectives proceeded at
5.30 p.m. June 3 to the Kuo Hwa Middle School where it was
ascertained that Tsu's home address was 201 Penang Road.
Tsiang's home at 6/234 Mapai Road was then visited and the
premises searched. A large quantity of anti-Japanese
literature, booklets, brochures, pamphlets and miscellaneous
notes were seized as was one mimeograph duplicator in good
condition. These articles were subsequently removed to
Headquarters. A summarized list of the seizures made at
this address is attached herewith.
During the course of the search of these premises Tsiang
stated that Tsu possibly might be at 4/234 Mapai Road, which
housed the Wei Hai ( 惠西 ) Primary School where the two
of them conducted an afternoon class for very poor children.
Tsiang's suggestion was acted upon and Tsu was arrested at
6 p.m June 3 at 4/234 Mapai Road, the indicated address.
A thorough search of this address failed to reveal any
documents of a political nature. Tsu Tsieu (朱脩 ),
aged 20, a native of Pootung, single, student, admitted
that his home address was 201 Penang Road but subsequent
enquiries revealed that this location was beyond the
jurisdiction of the Settlement and no attempt was made to
search the place concerned.
Tsu also admitted that the anti-Japanese literature found
in Tsiang's home had been obtained by him at 3 p.m. June 3
from one Tseu at 120/118 Yates Road. He further acknowledged
having handed Tsiang the literature and receipt found in the

在搜查该处所期间，蒋称朱可能位于马白路4/234号，该处为惠西小学，两人曾在此为极贫困儿童开设下午补习班。警方采纳了蒋的建议，并于6月3日下午6时在上述地址马白路4/234号逮捕了朱。对该地址的彻底搜查未发现任何具有政治性质的文件。朱脩（Tsu Tsieu），20岁，浦东人，未婚，学生，承认其住址为槟榔路201号，但随后的调查显示该地点超出租界管辖范围，因此未尝试搜查该处。
朱还承认，在蒋家中发现的反日文献是他于6月3日下午3时从耶茨路120/118号的周（Tseu）处获得的。他进一步承认已将文献及收据交给蒋，后者在被捕时

    In regard to ,his remarks vis-a-vis Tseu, Tsu amplified
this statement by declaring that this man had supplied large
quantities of anti-Japanese publications to various persons
in the past.    In view of this piece of news, it was decided
to proceed immediately to 120/118 Yates Road, but upon arrival
there, the wanted man, it was learned, had left the premises
a few minutes prior to the raiding party's arrival, having
received what can only be termed a suspicious telephone message
whilst the party of detectives was en route.    Although an
attempt had been made to remove all traces of anything relating
to anti-Japanese literature and/or activities and national
salvation affairs, a few copies of recent issues of "Unity"
were found as were several miscellaneous notes of such a nature
as to prove conclusively that Tseu was acting as a supplier of
subversive publications to various persons.    A summarized
list of the seizures made at this address is forwarded herewith.

    The search was conducted in the presence of a female
servant who declined to reveal her name but who stated, however,
that Tseu's full name was Tseu Vung Ziang (周文庠).    A
photograph of this man was found during the search and handed
to C.D.S. 89 (Special Branch) who was left on the premises
with instructions to effect his arrest should he return.

    Chengtu Road Station was apprised of the search made in
its district and a brief summary of the facts relating to the
activities carried out on June 3 was made known to Louza
Station, in whose district the initial arrest was made on May 29.

    关于他对周的陈述，朱补充说明称，此人过去曾向各类人员提供大量反日出版物。鉴于这一消息，警方决定立即前往耶茨路120/118号，但到达那里后得知，目标人物在搜捕小组抵达前几分钟已离开该处，据信他在侦探小组途中接到了一通只能称为可疑的电话。尽管有人试图清除所有与反日文献和/或活动及救国事务有关的痕迹，但仍发现了数份近期出版的《团结》杂志，以及若干性质足以确凿证明周充当颠覆性出版物供应商的杂项笔记。随函转发在该地址查获物品的摘要清单。

    搜查是在一名女佣在场的情况下进行的，她拒绝透露姓名，但声称周的全名为周文庠（Tseu Vung Ziang）。搜查中发现了此人的照片，并交给了特别部第89号中国侦探（C.D.S. 89），该侦探被留在现场，奉命若周返回即行逮捕。

    成都路分局已获知在其辖区内进行的搜查情况，并与老闸分局通报了6月3日行动的相关事实摘要，首次逮捕是在5月29日于老闸分局辖区内执行的。

Interrogation of Tsiang and Tsu at Headquarters
during the night of June 3/4 revealed that they were
associated with the Students' Circles' National Salvation
Association and as such were disseminating anti-Japanese
and national salvation propaganda. According to Tsiang
the meeting place of the staff members of this particular
National Salvation group is the Medhurst College, Medhurst
Road.

In regard to the copies of various publications
seized at 6/234 Mapai Road it was ascertained from
Tsiang and Tsu that the latter intended to distribute the
anti-Japanese literature among the students of the Kuo
Hwa ( 國華 ) Middle School of which both are student
members, Tsu being responsible to the Students' Circles'
National Salvation Association for this distribution.

Detailed statements of these two men will beforwarded
in due course.

Subject Anti-Japanese and communistic publications - distribution
through newsvendors.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford

P.A. (S.B.)
〔左侧手写批注：June ... he views that ... the matter of the Soviet ... is difficult ... but a ... with should be kept ... any definite ... upon ... for further instructions.〕

Information was obtained recently that one of the
principal means of distributing certain publications in
Shanghai was through secret sale by newsvendors. In particular
this information referred to the brochures:-
1) "Labour" (anti-Japanese)
2) "Unity" (anti-Japanese) and
3) "Emancipation" (anti-Japanese and communistic).

Enquiries coupled with general observation conducted by
members of this office revealed that a male Chinese aged
about 38 years was in the habit of carrying packets of these
publications and delivering them to various street-corner
newsvendors with whom he had made previous arrangements
for their disposal. Investigation reveals that he sold the
papers for one cent per copy to the vendors, who in turn
retailed them at two and/or three cents each. Diligent
efforts were made by certain of the vendors in accordance
with confidential instructions received from this office, to
discreetly ascertain from the Chinese who brought the papers
further details about himself, the manner in which he
received the brochures, how and where they were printed,
etc. etc., but it appeared evident that the Chinese was
extremely well guarded in all his replies for no information
of any material value to this office could be secured.

At 2.30 p.m. May 29, 1938, this Chinese was under
surveillance in the Louza district when, realizing that
he was being shadowed, he attempted to evade his pursuer's
attentions by running as fast as he could along Amoy Road
in the direction of Yu Ya Ching Road. C.D.S.89 of this
office, who was following him, caught him near Yu Ya Ching

近期获得情报，在上海分销某些出版物的主要手段之一是通过报贩秘密销售。具体而言，该情报涉及以下小册子：
1) 《劳工》（反日）
2) 《团结》（反日）以及
3) 《解放》（反日及共产主义）。

本处成员进行的查询及一般观察显示，一名约38岁的中国男子习惯携带这些出版物的包裹，并将其交付给各个街角报贩，此前他已与这些报贩就处置事宜达成安排。调查显示，他以每份一分的价格将报纸卖给报贩，报贩再以每份两分和/或三分的价格零售。根据本处收到的机密指示，某些报贩努力谨慎地向送报的中国男子探询关于其本人、接收小册子的方式、印刷地点及方式等更多细节，但显然该中国男子在所有回答中都极为谨慎，因此本处未能获取任何具有实质价值的情报。

    自去年10月10日起，他开始前往西区社会中心，在那里聆听了大量关于当时局势、抗战及救国事务的讲座。在那里，他结识了胡（Hu），此人由文化界救国会指派在社会中心工作。在他的影响下，袁某后来开始与他一起在文化界协会工作。在与该组织联系期间，袁某被介绍给另一位救国主义者唐友瑚（Tang Yeu Woo）。唐某与袁某保持联系直到今年二月，直到前者生病，直到四月袁某未再见任何与运动有关的人。四月唐某再次出现，并将袁某介绍给曾札（Tseng Tsuh），后者指导袁某的救国活动约六周。5月13日，本处已知其为职业界救国会调查科前科长的曾某前往汉口，但在此之前，袁某又被介绍给

    In the list of literature seized from Yuan's
person on May 29 (Appendix A), it will be observed from
item No.1 that he has been issuing copies of "Unity,"
"Labour" and "Emancipation" since at least March of this
year, whilst No.5 contains a list of workers of the
Hung Tsang Cotton Mill who, at various times, have
contributed towards the fund for "Labour."

    It is of interest to note that Yuan Ken-sung has
been identified by a secret agent of this office as one
of the leading figures in the now defunct "Western District
Young Men and Women's National Salvation Association" in
the Western District Social Centre.    In November and
December, 1937 he was the person who supplied copies of
the "Emancipation" (communistic in nature) (which was then
a secret publication mailed to Shanghai from Sian and which
could not be obtained locally).    Owing to the extremist
activities of the association, the Western District Social
Centre was ordered by the Municipal Police to close at the
end of December, 1937.

    On December 28, 1937, a secret gala meeting of
members of the National Salvation Association was held in
the Chinese Y.W.C.A. School for Female Workers, 4434 Yu

已安排将这些摊位的业主带到本局，他们将受到关于不得交易反日刊物的严厉警告，并被要求签署保证书，承诺不再从事此类活动。

在5月29日从袁身上搜获的刊物清单（附录A）中，从第1项可以看出，他至少自今年三月起一直在发行《团结》、《劳工》和《解放》刊物，而第5项包含了一份鸿章棉厂工人的名单，这些工人在不同时期曾为《劳工》刊物基金捐款。

值得注意的是，本局一名秘密特工已指认袁耕莘是现已解散的“西区男女青年救国协会”在西区社会中心的主要人物之一。1937年11月和12月，他是提供《解放》（具有共产主义性质）副本的人（当时这是一份秘密出版物，从西安邮寄至上海，无法在当地获得）。由于该协会的极端活动，工部局警务处于1937年12月底下令关闭西区社会中心。

1937年12月28日，救国协会成员在位于罗宾森路裕庆里（Yu Ching Li）4434号的中国基督教女青年会女工学校举行了一次秘密盛大会议，时间为晚上7点至10点半，约有100人出席，由被捕者袁耕莘主持。

List of literature, documents, etc. seized at the home
of Yuan Ken Sung (袁耕莘 ), at No.9 Hung Shou Fang
(鴻壽坊), Mapai Road near Ferry Road at 3.20 p.m. 30/5/38.

1. A letter addressed to Yuan ( 袁 ) by one Yao Yu Hu
(饒友瑚 ) informing Yuan that 6 copies of "Unity"
have been sent to him.

2. A brief note dated April 12 addressed to Yuan by Tseng
Tsuh ( 曾 朴 ) (formerly Chief of the Investigation
Dept. of the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association) arranging an interview between them.

3. A brief note dated May 6 addressed to Yuan by Tseng
Tsuh explaining the cause of his failure to call on him.

4. A letter dated Tuesday afternoon addressed to Yuan by
Yao Yu Hu asking the former to call on him between 12
noon and 1 p.m. on any date at (name of place cut out).

5. A letter dated January 17 addressed to Yuan by Yao Yu Hu
asking Yuan to supply a list of names, age, and other
particulars of the members of the three sections.

6. A note dated April 30 addressed to Yuan by the Western
District Social Centre requesting his presence at a
meeting in connection with the education of poor children
to be held at 10 a.m. Sunday, May 1.

7. A draft of an article relating to the attitude to be
adopted during the war of resistance. (This draft was
found on a desk in Yuan's room during the raid)

8. Paper slips bearing names of persons receiving copies
of certain periodicals.

9. A booklet entitled "Stalinism and Bolshevism," purporting
to emanate from the Trotsky Clique of the Chinese Communist
Party.

10. A periodical entitled "Pu Hua" ( 火 花 ) (Spark),
Volume 3, Issue No.2, dated May 10, 1936, purporting to
emanate from the Chinese Communist League.

11. A leaflet entitled "China and Japan" dated July 30, 1937,
purporting to emanate from the Trotsky Clique. 1 copy.

12. A leaflet entitled "Arm the People to Defend Shanghai and
to Promote a General War of Resistance on All Fronts"
purporting to emanate from Chinese Communist League on
October 28. 1 copy.

13. A book entitled "United Front and the Fate of Stalin Party"
issued in June, 1937 by the Chinese Communist League.

1938年5月30日下午3时20分，在靠近渡船路的马派路（Mapai Road）鸿寿坊9号袁耕莘（Yuan Ken Sung）家中搜获的文献、文件等清单。

1. 饶友瑚（Yao Yu Hu）致袁（Yuan）的一封信，告知袁已向其寄送6份《团结》。

2. 曾朴（Tseng Tsuh，前职业界救国会调查部主任）于4月12日致袁的一张便条，安排双方会面。

3. 曾朴（Tseng Tsuh）于5月6日致袁的一张便条，解释其未能拜访的原因。

4. 饶友瑚（Yao Yu Hu）于某周二下午致袁的一封信，请袁在任何一天的中午12点至下午1点之间到（地点名称被剪去）拜访他。

5. 饶友瑚（Yao Yu Hu）于1月17日致袁的一封信，请袁提供三个部门成员的姓名、年龄及其他详细资料清单。

6. 西区社会中心于4月30日致袁的一张便条，请其出席定于5月1日星期日上午10时举行的关于贫困儿童教育的会议。

7. 一篇关于抗战期间应采取的态度之文章草稿。（此草稿是在突袭期间于袁的房间书桌上发现的）

8. 载有接收某些刊物副本人员姓名的纸条。

9. 一本名为《斯大林主义与布尔什维克主义》的小册子，声称出自中国共产党托派集团。

10. 一本名为《火花》（Pu Hua）的刊物，第3卷第2期，日期为1936年5月10日，声称出自中国共产主义者同盟。

11. 一份名为《中国与日本》的传单，日期为1937年7月30日，声称出自托派集团。1份。

12. 一份名为《武装民众保卫上海并推动全面抗战》的传单，声称出自中国共产主义者同盟，日期为10月28日。1份。

13. 一本名为《统一战线与斯大林党的命运》的书，由中国共产主义者同盟于1937年6月出版。

| | At 2.35 p.m. May 29, C.D.S. 89 (Special Branch) and C.P.C. 1359 brought to the station one Yan Keng Sung (袁耕舜), a male Chinese, aged 38, a native of Hangchow, residing at 9 Hun Shou Fon (鸿寿坊), Ferry Road. This person has been the subject of Special Branch surveillance for the past three weeks being suspected of being involved in the dissemination of anti-Japanese literature and thought to be connected with the National Salvation movement. | |
| | At 2.30 p.m. today whilst C.D.S. 89 was shadowing the man on Amoy Road and generally observing his movements, he attempted to escape his pursuer, but was caught after a short chase on Amoy Road near Yu Ya Ching Road. D.S. Pitts and D.S.I. Kao Yen Kao of the Special Branch attended and later took the man to Special Branch headquarters where he was thoroughly interrogated as to his recent activities. It was ascertained that he was working for the Labourer's National Salvation Association in the Western Shanghai District and that he was also acting as a teacher at the Chinese Y.M.C.A. Western Social Centre on Robison Road, from which organisation he has been regularly receiving copies of publications entitled "Unity", "Labour" and "Emancipation", all anti-Japanese in tone and which he has been selling for one cent per | |

S.1 Special Branch,
December 30, 1937.

National Salvation Movement - arrests
and seizure of propaganda.

At 3 p.m., December 30, a party of Police from
Chengtu Road under D.I. Hill, D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken and
D.S. McKeown, acting upon the instructions of the
D.C. (Special Branch) visited room 218, 749 Bubbling
Well Road, suspected of being a depot of the national
salvation association. A large quantity of Chinese
flags, anti-Japanese greeting cards, national salvation
propaganda, and a mimeograph machine were seized. The
seizure was removed to the Special Branch and is at
present in process of classification. Present in the
office at the time of the police visit were three male
Chinese namely :

(1) Wong Ming Yang(王明陽 ), salesman for the
China National Insurance Company;
(2) Yang Yuan Kong(楊元康 ), shroff in the employ
of the Foch Rubber Company, 490 Avenue Foch;
(3) Tseu Zung Teh(周成德 ), unemployed.

These three persons were taken to Chengtu Road Station
and full statements were obtained (copies attached).

The 1st accused Wong Ming Yang, was definitely
connected with the National Salvation Movement. He admits
being formerly a member of the Foreign Owned Firms Chinese
Employees Lien Nyi Society which formed part of the
Vocational Circles National Salvation Association which
was dissolved following the withdrawal of Chinese troops
from Shanghai. He agreed to participate in the revival
of the National Salvation Movement at the request of one
page_data.zh:
副本

S.1 特科，
1937年12月30日。

救国运动 - 逮捕及查扣宣传品。

12月30日下午3时，成都路捕房的一队警员，在希尔督察（D.I. Hill）、高延根副督察（D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken）及麦基恩副探长（D.S. McKeown）带领下，遵照特科副巡长（D.C. (Special Branch)）的指示，搜查了静安寺路749号218室，该处涉嫌为救国协会的据点。查获大量中国国旗、抗日贺年卡、救国宣传品及一台油印机。查获物品已移送特科，目前正在进行分类整理。警方到访时，办公室内有三名华籍男子在场，即：

(1) 王明陽 (Wong Ming Yang)，中国保险公司推销员；
(2) 楊元康 (Yang Yuan Kong)，福煦路490号福煦橡胶公司（Foch Rubber Company）出纳员；
(3) 周成德 (Tseu Zung Teh)，无业。

此三人被带往成都路捕房，并获取了完整供词（附副本）。

第一被告王明陽，确与救国运动有关联。他承认曾是外商华员联谊社（Foreign Owned Firms Chinese Employees Lien Nyi Society）成员，该社隶属于职业界救国会，后者在中国军队撤离上海后解散。他应蒙太班路（Rue Montauban）法亚保险公司（Assurance Franco-Asiatique）买办杨延修（Yang Yien Siu）之请，同意参与救国运动的复兴工作。

page_data.en:
-2-

Yang Yien Siu (楊延修), compradore of the Assurance
Franco-Asiatique, Rue Montauban. Yang, a person of some
social standing, appears to be a leading light in the
present movement. His residential address is not known.
Wong Ming Yang admitted that he was engaged in delivering
articles including flags and anti-Japanese greeting cards
on behalf of the National Salvation Association.

The second accused Yang Yuan Kong admits having been
a member of the Vocational Circles National Salvation
Association prior to the withdrawal of Chinese troops,
and states that he was requested on December 30 to take
an active part in the movement. His statement that he
has taken no part in the movement is belied by the fact
that he was in the office at the time of the Police visit.

The third accused Tseu Zung Teh states that a
friend found employment for him in the office at room 218,
distributing cotton vests at a monthly wage of $6.00.
Later he states that a person in the office told him to
distribute 300 greeting cards and 3,000 Chinese National
Flags to all who applied for them. Although Tseu denies
all knowledge of the organization, he is of average
intelligence and doubtless realized the importance of the
work in which he was engaged.

Consequent upon detectives being left to maintain a
watch over the premises, seven male Chinese were arrested
between 6 p.m. and 12 midnight, December 30, namely:-
page_data.zh:
-2-

杨氏具有一定社会地位，似乎是当前运动的骨干分子。其住址不详。王明陽承认，他受救国协会委托，从事包括旗帜和抗日贺年卡在内的物品递送工作。

第二被告楊元康承认，在中国军队撤离前曾是职业界救国会成员，并称于12月30日被要求积极参与该运动。他声称自己未参与运动，但警方到访时他身在办公室这一事实戳穿了他的谎言。

第三被告周成德称，一位朋友为他在218室办公室谋得一份差事，负责分发棉背心，月薪6.00元。随后他又称，办公室内有人让他向所有申领者分发300张贺年卡和3,000面中国国旗。尽管周成德否认对该组织有任何了解，但他智力中等，无疑意识到其所从事工作的重要性。

由于留派探员监视该处所，12月30日下午6时至午夜12时之间，七名华籍男子被捕，即：-

page_data.en:
-3-
(4) Zee Tseng Yue ( 徐振裕 ), unemployed;
(5) Wong Yih ( 王乙 ), alias Wong Ai Yue
( 王衡遠 ), unemployed;
(6) Loo Chi Yuan ( 羅哲原 ), apprentice;
(7) Ling Lien-fang ( 凌聯芳 ), partner in a flour
shop;
(8) Li Nyih-jing ( 李業勤 ), unemployed;
(9) Co Ching-wen ( 鄒錦文 ), unemployed;
(10) Loo Wen-lai ( 盧文瀾 ), unemployed.

The 4th accused Zee Tseng Yue admits having joined
the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association in
August, 1937 but states that his activities were confined
to the collection of funds from friends or relatives on
behalf of the association in September and October, 1937.
He denies that he is taking any part in the present movement,
stating that he was merely residing in room 218, but this
statement is open to doubt from the fact that he was a
former member and found in the office with propaganda much
in evidence. Zee Tseng Yue mentions the name of one
Zung Tsing ( 程俊 ), address unknown, clerk in the Customs
Employees Club as being a member of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association.

The 5th accused Wong Yih, alias Wong Ai Yue admits
that prior to the outbreak of hostilities, he was a member
of the Vocational Circles National Salvation Association
and was employed in the office of the association. He
states that he was merely residing with friends in room 218,

第四被告徐振裕承认曾于1937年8月加入职业界救国会，但称其活动仅限于1937年9月和10月代表该会向亲友募集资金。他否认参与当前的运动，称自己 merely 居住在218室，但鉴于他是前成员，且在办公室内被发现时周围有明显宣传品，此说法令人怀疑。徐振裕提及海关职员俱乐部（Customs Employees Club）职员程俊（Zung Tsing，地址不详）也是职业界救国会成员。

第五被告王乙，化名王衡遠，承认在战事爆发前曾是职业界救国会成员，并在该会办公室任职。他称自己只是与朋友一同居住在218室，

page_data.en:
-4-

but as in the cese of the 4th accused, this statement is
open to doubt.

The 6th accused, Loo Chi Yuan, is a friend of the
4th accused, and visited room 218. He denies that he is
participating in the National Salvation Movement.

The 7th accused denies that he is participating
in the movement. He is a friend of the 3rd accused,
Tseu Zung Teh and explains his visit to room 218 by
stating that a loan was being contracted.

The 8th accused Li Myih-jing ( as in the case of the
7th accused), states that he is a friend of the 3rd accused,
and was invited to reside in room 218. He denies that he
is participating in any activities.

The 9th accused Oo Ching Wen is known to the 3rd
and the 7th accused, but denies that his visit to room 218
had any untoward significance.

The arrest of the 10th accused Loo Wen-lai appears
to be of particular importance inasmuch as his examination
and the documents in his possession lead to the belief of
the recrudescence of communism. His statement is typical
of those previously obtained from members of the Communist
Party and documents in his possession which have not yet
been translated are not those ordinarily found on members
of National Salvation organizations.

Of immediate importance is a mimeographed document
entitled "General Outline of Work during the Propaganda
Period," a translation of which follows :-

但与第四被告的情况一样，此说法令人怀疑。

第六被告羅哲原是第四被告的朋友，曾到访218室。他否认参与救国运动。

第七被告否认参与该运动。他是第三被告周成德的朋友，解释其到访218室的原因是正在商谈一笔借款。

第八被告李業勤（与第七被告情况相同），称自己是第三被告的朋友，受邀居住在218室。他否认参与任何活动。

第九被告鄒錦文为第三及第七被告所认识，但否认其到访218室有任何不当意义。

第十被告盧文瀾的被捕似乎尤为重要，因为对其审讯及其随身文件使人相信共产主义死灰复燃。他的供词是此前从共产党成员处获得的典型供词，而他身上尚未翻译的文件也并非通常在救国组织成员身上发现的那些。

其中一份立即引起重视的油印文件题为《宣传期工作大纲》，译文如下：-

The conference will decide the number of members
to be mobilized for the propaganda movement, fund

(Three persons to form a group).

(2) The work during the Propaganda Period :
General
Proceed with the fund raising campaign for the
relief of refugees.
Enforce anti-Japanese propaganda.
Persuade all shops to hoist national flags
on New Year Day.
Distribute paper slogans on New Year Day among
relatives, friends in shops, alleyways, schools
and refugee camps.
Prepare wall papers.
Hold separate meetings in schools, shops,
refugee camps, factories, take oaths not to
become traitors, not to purchase Japanese goods.
Distribute New Year Cards of an anti-Japanese
nature.
At 10 a.m. New Year Day, mobilize members, to
go to various alleyways and streets and shout slogan:
"Long Live the Republic of China! "

根据11时至午夜12时间从第十被告处获得的情报，成都路捕房及特科探员走访了青岛路77号一名叫凌亦生（Ling Yih Sing）的人的住所，此人据称是救国运动中的重要人物。凌不在家，但在楼下房间，以及据第十被告称由凌租住的楼上房间内，发现了大量抗日书籍、救国宣传品及一台油印机。这些文献正在

classification. In the upstairs room were found two
females who were brought to the station namely :
(11) King Jing (金瑾), student;
(12) Ho Ping (何平), alias Ho Ying (何英)
school teacher.

The 11th accused, King Jing, when interrogated told
a tissue of lies, contradicting her statements repeatedly.
Although no definite evidence can be produced against
her, she appears to be involved in the National Salvation
movement.

The 12th accused Ho Ping alias Ho Ying admits that
she was a member of a group which advocates National
Salvation work, and functions secretly at 77 Tsingtao Road.
She was paid by Ling Yih Sing (mentioned above). She
mentions the name of one Tsu Shih-tung (朱澤東), who
is also involved in the movement at the same address.

The ten males and two females are being detained in
Chengtu Road Station pending further instructions.

第十二被告何平，化名何英，承认她是主张开展救国工作的一个团体的成员，该团体在青岛路77号秘密活动。她的薪水由上述凌亦生支付。她提及朱澤東（Tsu Shih-tung）的名字，此人也在同一地址参与该运动。

十名男性和两名女性正被拘留于成都路捕房，等待进一步指示。

Wong Ming Yang (王明揚)
Ningpo                                      D.S. McKeown
Chengtu Rd. Stn.      30/12/37              D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken

    My name is Wong Ming Yang, aged 24, a native of Ningpo,
and married. I am a salesman of the China National Insurance
Company, China Land Bank Building, corner of Peking and Kiangse
Roads, and reside at 20 Kiu Foh Li, Mandalay Road. I am a
member of the Foreign Owned Firms Chinese Employees Lien
Nyi Society, formerly situated at 115 Hankow Road and now at
Pootung Bank Building (2nd floor), corner of Avenue Ed. VII
and Honan Road, which was part of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association.    Automatically I became
member of the national salvation association, which was
dissolved following the withdrawal of the Chinese forces.
    At the end of November 1937, Yang Yien Siu (楊延修),
compradore of the Assurance Franco-Asiatique, Rue Montauban,
and concurrently a staff member of the Organization Section of
the Foreign Owned Firms Chinese Employees' Lien Nyi Society,
asked me to assist him in conducting national salvation works/
among refugees. He belongs to the Vocational Circles National
Salvation Association, with secret offices the addresses of
which I do not know. Although I am a member of this organiza-
tion, I merely receive orders from Yang. The work among the
refugees is a part of the programme of the Vocational Circles
National Salvation Association. My principal work is to
deliver articles, including flags and cards. Although a
number of persons work in this organization, I only know the
following persons :-
1. Yang Yien Siu
2. Yang Yuan Kong (in custody).
